utterances.text: Your Honours, the explosive residue and blood examinations, those samples were collected prior to my arrival at the Tribunal. I did assist the Netherlands Forensic Institute in providing those samples and returning those samples and I did review their reports. In a similar fashion Dr. Brown's reports were reviewed by myself and I, on occasion, would accompany Dr. Brown to various sites and was present when he took his samples, and I spoke to him about his results.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, are we at the time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed we are. Mr. Manning, you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Take a break of 20 minutes or come back at quarter past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the witness please the escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: One last question as to the surface remains before moving on. These surface remains that you have said were recovered by the BiH authorities, am I correct, all total we're talking about, what, under 200? Under 100? What is the figure, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the figure. I don't recall the figure.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. Then we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At -- if we can call up 65 ter number 1D1111, and if we can look at page 61 of the same, which should correlate to transcript page 18962 of that underlying transcript. And if we can zoom in on lines 7 through 19.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: And, sir, I'd like to focus with you on this question and answer from the Popovic case again at line 7: "Just generally still, can you tell us whether there had been any evidence in any other graves that you've exhumed that the -- that there were soldiers comingled with civilians inside the graves? "A. We didn't find any significant number of uniforms to indicate military forces. We also did not find equipment in -- to indicate military forces. We did find some material and some very limited numbers of, say, a camouflage shirt or a military jacket. "No, to my recollection or knowledge, no individuals were found in a complete uniform. One pistol was located in the belt of an individual at Glogova. He wasn't wearing military clothing, and that pistol was in a loaded condition. I understand a grenade was found in 1996 in the sleeve of an individual, but apart from that, we did not find evidence of military artifacts or clothing amongst the dead." Sir, first of all, do you stand by this question and answer as being truthful and accurate as to the matters stated therein?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Now, you've as part of your investigation seen the statements of many of the Bosnian Muslim males from Srebrenica and I think you will agree with me that there are a significant number of statements talking about how members of the Bosnian Muslim column, whether armed or not, were in civilian rather than military uniforms. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That the majority of them were in civilian clothing? Yes, I would agree with that.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: And again, when you say in the previous answer that we read from Popovic that you did not find many in uniforms, et cetera, those observations would be limited to those graves exhumed by the ICTY personnel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw the clothing and artefacts from the ICTY graves. I did read some details in the Bosnian records.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I seek clarification of one of the previous answers. When you said that you'd agree with the majority of them were in civilian clothing, did you intend to say that the majority of the members of the Bosnian Muslim -- oh, it says "column," let me just see. Yes, majority of the column were in civilian clothing? Yes, I was a bit confused, Mr. Ivetic, because you -- no, I'm not confused. I shouldn't blame you for it. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Now, as to the lack of any military hardware, we've already talked about the process of sanitisation, or "asanacija." And I want to ask you, sir, given what you know, given your investigations, do you consider seriously that at a time of war when "asanacija" is being done to safe-guard the public from harm that could be occasioned by the presence of bodies, explosives, and weapons left in the open, would you consider it logical and reasonable that weapons would be knowingly buried with the bodies where scavengers could get ahold of them and where explosions could still take place?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're asking me if "asanacija" was conducted correctly, would they bury weapons with the bodies, I would say I doubt that. There may be circumstances where they do. If "asanacija," or clearing of the battle-field, is done correctly, I would assume that that would happen.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: You're going to have to clarify when you say, "I assume that would happen," you would assume --

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. That the weapons and explosives would be removed or protected. I can see a situation perhaps where a need to bury them quickly and they bury them completely, including their weapons, with the intention of recovering them later, but I'm not a military expert.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And if I could ask you, perhaps, from your professional career in the Australian police force when a body is found with a weapon next to it in the street, is the body interred or buried with that weapon or is the weapon safe-guarded in some other location?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it is.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you do have information that at least some of the bodies that were found in the graves that were not excavated by the ICTY did not or perhaps did not relate to Srebrenica; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can look at 1D1112 in e-court, page 61 of that transcript, which should correlate to transcript page 19050 of the Popovic proceedings. And if we can focus on lines 16 through 19.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Rather than reading the whole thing, I'd like to see if I can refresh your recollection by reading your answers contained in that page of the transcript that says: "The Bljeceva 1 mass grave, which is not an ICTY mass grave, contains the remains of 39 individuals positively identified via DNA analysis as being missing following the fall of Srebrenica. It contains persons from Srebrenica as well as perhaps unconnected bodies." Does that refresh your recollection or --

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that evidence, but I accept that that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Okay. And would you accept that your recollection was perhaps better back when you testified in Popovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But your question was not that, Mr. Lukic. Your question was that -- I beg your pardon, Mr. Ivetic. I'm sorry, Mr. Lukic, if you are here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: He's not here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He's not here. Okay. "Now, you do have information that at least some of the bodies that were found in the graves that were not excavated by the ICTY did not or perhaps did not relate to Srebrenica," and I emphasise "relate." Now, what you are quoting here, he does indicate that they did relate but there may have been other people within those graves. But they did relate to Srebrenica. "The Bljeceva 1 mass grave which is not an ICTY mass grave contains the remains of 39 individuals positively identified via DNA analysis as being missing following the fall of Srebrenica."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps I caused an error by skipping to the answer and not reading the question. If you read from line 9 of transcript, it reads: "'Tuzla canton court Prosecution file," and it gives a number, "relates to this grave and indicates that this grave also contained the remains of bodies unconnected with the fall of Srebrenica" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That is not what you quoted to the witness at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I understand. That's what I said. So I take responsibility for that confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can look at page 81 of this transcript which should correlate to transcript page 19070 of the underlying Popovic transcript. And if we can focus on line 23 through 25 and then it will be lines 1 through 8 on the next page once we go there.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Again, sir, I invite you to follow along as I read the question and answers and then I'll have some questions about it. "Q. Okay. Now, being a police officer for 24 years and having worked murder details, for example, do you believe and agree with me that a pathologist must be independent and objective when coming to the manner," if we can go to the next page, resuming the reading, "and cause of death? "A. Yes, as should the -- as should the police investigator. "Q. Okay. And would you also agree with me that a pathologist must maintain that independence and objectivity, and that neither Defence counsel nor a prosecutor should be allowed to assist or encourage them in the cause or manner of death? "A. If you're asking if a Defence counsel or Prosecutor should be allowed to assist or encourage in the cause or manner of death, no." Answer -- pardon me, end of the quotation. Sir, the question I have for you is: Do you stand by this prior testimony as something that is both truthful and accurate, that you would testify to again if asked the same questions today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the question is asking for opinion and judgement, so you could ask the witness whether he has the same opinion or same judgement --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- not whether it's accurate or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. You're correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You could even wonder whether such a question should be put to a witness of fact, but I leave that aside.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Do you still believe the same way or hold the same position that we now read back from Popovic?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, in that context, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Do you believe that as an investigator of the Prosecution you were empowered to undertake all measures to obtain a conviction even if it meant being untruthful yourself?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I understand the question correctly, and I take some objection, my job wasn't to obtain a conviction. My job was to obtain the evidence and hopefully present it in court, and that's your decision or the Court's decision. I have never been untruthful in this court or any other court, and I believe that my job was to be as independent and impartial as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, if you could please ask facts of the witness rather than try to pass judgement on the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask him this factual question then.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Have you ever been untruthful in the course of your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He's just told you a few minutes ago he has never been.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the courtroom, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Have you ever been untruthful in the course of a witness interview to attempt to obtain information to be used by the Office of the Prosecutor in court proceedings?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe I've been untruthful with the intention of obtaining information. I would strive to tell the truth as much as possible. Certainly on occasion you would not tell the witness everything and I would try to ensure that what I told the witness was correct as far as I could tell that witness. And I would strive not to provide them with information which was false.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I come back to you, Mr. Ivetic, again in the previous sentence the witness said: "I have never been untruthful in this court or in any other court, and I believe my job was to be as independent and impartial as possible."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So even outside the courtroom. So what you are suggesting to him, outside the courtroom, was already answered by his assertion of impartiality.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: I think to be fair I'm going to have to go through the entire procedure from beginning to end.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can look at 1D1113, please, in e-court. And it is the 70th page in e-court, which should correlate to transcript page 19140 of the underlying -- I apologise. It should be three pages back or four pages back. And one page before at the middle of the page and we'll be getting to this page eventually, but from line 14 and onwards. We'll take it step by step.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: And if you'll follow along with me, sir, this was your examination in the Popovic trial by one of the Defence teams. "Q. And you've been at pains, I think particularly when Mr. Meek was cross-examining you, to emphasise how fair, honest and objective you were in conducting interviews with the very witnesses -- with the very many witnesses and suspects you interviewed. That's correct, isn't it? "A. I explained to Mr. Meek that that's the way I conduct my duties. "Q. Would you agree with me that it's part of your interviewing style to make the suspect or witness perfectly aware of the material at your disposal? "A. Your Honours, again this is quite general, but if I am in a position to tell the suspect certain things, I will. That's not to say that if I have a piece of information, that I will tell that person that I have that information. I indicated I wouldn't lie, but it's not always," if we can go to the next page, lines 1 through 2, continuing with the reading, "the case that I would tell them everything that I knew or everything that I had. But, again, that's being very general." First, do you still stand behind this prior testimony?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Does this refresh your recollection of the discussion of the interview that you conducted with Mr. Milorad Bircakovic?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. Your Honours, I was asked about my comments to a witness in a previous trial and I explained that I had said to the witness that I had personally exhumed thousands of bodies and that we had evidence which showed executions taking place at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Were those things that you said to the witness truthful at the time that you said them?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've thought about that since, and I can say that they are. I did personally exhume thousands of bodies as part of that team. I stood in the grave and I helped carry the bodies from the graves and I worked for six years on those exhumations -- four years on those exhumations. And I believe we did have evidence and we do have evidence of executions taking place at the time. Certainly, the video of the Kravica warehouse shows individuals being executed in the warehouse. And as a previous witness has indicated, there is evidence of bodies laying on the ground at Kravica warehouse that had been killed by Mr. Erdemovic and his comrades. So yes, I overexaggerated, I overstated, but I believe that the facts are true. And I recall that my position was to make sure that the witness, who was a witness, understood clearly that we had a wealth of information and that he very strongly understood our position.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: You just mentioned Mr. Erdemovic and his comrades at Kravica warehouse. Was that really the result of your investigation?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, my apologies. At --

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Branjevo --

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Branjevo Military Farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can move ahead three pages from the present point in that 65 ter document in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: I'd like to re-visit what you had said at the Popovic trial so we have the full picture of it. From lines 1 through to 17, sir. At number 1 the question posed is: "Why did you tell him all that? "A. Clearly, I'm indicating to him that we had a substantial amount of information, that it was in his interest to tell the truth. Clearly, I was conducting an interview. I suspected, as many of them did, that he would lie, and I was trying to give him as much information as possible that we had. "Now, I must make comment on two points. I wasn't present for the exhumations at those graves. And you asked me about the aerial imagery of executions, and clearly that's not correct. When I spoke about the aerial image of executions, in the Branjevo Military Farm photographs you can see what I believe and know to be bodies, and I take that as a valid comment, that that image shows bodies that have been executed. And I don't know why I indicated that I personally exhumed those bodies, knowing that I wasn't there in 1996. I would say that I haven't checked this interview against the record, the actual tape, but I accept the majority of what was said there. I can see that there are one or two words missing, but I accept that I said those things." Does now this and what you told us in the courtroom just prior to me asking this contain the entirety of your answer as to why you told factually incorrect things to this witness during this witness interview?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that that represents my position and why I said those things, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in relation to the training that you underwent at the Office of the Prosecutor, and I would even extend it back further to the Australian police, were you taught that for interviews of witnesses or suspects it was okay to misstate facts?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not taught that.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I put it to you, sir, that you want to see Mr. Mladic in the courtroom hearing a guilty verdict because you believe that he murdered people. Am I correct about you?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not sure if the Court wants to hear my personal view of the matter. I've already stated that I undertook my duties in an impartial manner, and I believe I sought to show evidence no matter whether it was exculpatory or the reverse. I believe that's my official position, and I don't know if the Court wants to hear my personal views.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Manning, the Court does not want to hear your personal views. But it does seem as if Mr. Ivetic wants to hear them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. If I can go back to the question --

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: I'll repeat it for you, if you like.

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: I put it to you, sir, that you want to see Mr. Mladic in the courtroom hearing a guilty verdict because you believe that he murdered people. Am I correct about this?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's correct, although I would say I want to see him in the courtroom and evidence presented, and if that evidence is sufficient - and I believe it is - that he be convicted for murdering men and boys, individuals.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Would you ever misrepresent facts in order to obtain a conviction of General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I would not. And in the example that you've provided, I don't believe I even approached that. As I said, I believe I exaggerated and the facts behind that are correct. I did exhume thousands of bodies and there is evidence of executions taking place.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: I would like to take a few moments to review a video with you that was just disclosed to us by the Prosecution 48 hours ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We do have the original transcript as provided by the provider, and it has been uploaded into e-court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the record, I'd just like to make clear that this is a video available from a very public source --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I wasn't implying that it was -- that it was a violation of any sort of the disclosure. But the transcript is in e-court and has been, I believe, given to all the booths. And if I can preface it by saying there is one part that I note where on the screen they are showing parts of the Srebrenica trial video and there are, I believe, subtitles or translations of that video --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Registrar informs the Chamber that only one copy was provided in the French language to the French booth and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If the booths can assist, I personally delivered to the English and the B/C/S, if they can confirm that they have those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I see somebody nodding in this booth here, showing a piece of paper, another one there -- I can't see the rest -- the stenographer is throwing her hands in the air.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Oh, I can -- with the assistance of the usher, I could provide a copy for the stenographer as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure that I'm getting any response from those booths there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's my understanding that the French booth is on that side and the English and B/C/S are behind us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There are two booths here. One must be the French, the other one must be some other language.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I don't know which one is which. That's why I asked for assistance to getting it to the French booths. I don't know how we can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. We're not hearing from them. I will assume that they are okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And as I was saying, there is -- there does appear to be a section of the interview with the journalist where portions of the Srebrenica trial video that we've used in this case, and that's been viewed time and again, is present and those sections do not appear in the transcript as provided by the media outlet that produced this documentary. So I wanted to bring that to everyone's attention. I'm not intending to rely on anything as translated in the subtitles or in the audio relating to the Srebrenica trial video. I want to focus only on the words said by the journalist and by Mr. Manning. And that's the introduction I have for this video. And it is 1D1126 and the first segment I'd like to show is from 2 minutes and 14 seconds to 3 minutes and 53 seconds. And, Your Honours, are we still showing them twice? I'm prepared to do so if that is the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think, yeah, we might as well show them twice because you see --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- relying on the text between Mr. Manning and the journalist.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So then we will play the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "Liam Bartlett: Dean Manning, Australian federal policeman, has spent six years as an investigator in one of the biggest crime scenes in the world, preparing the case against General Mladic. He will testify how Mladic incited his men to hunt down, capture, and execute Muslims. "Ratko Mladic: [Voiceover] 'The time has come to take revenge on the Muslims.' "Dean: He said that here in front of his men. "Liam Bartlett: What does that mean to his men? "Dean: 'Take revenge' - kill them, and that's what they did. "Liam Bartlett: The murderous directive was carried out with such cold-blooded efficiency, it was over in just three days - some of it even recorded by the killers for their home videos. Srebrenica was sealed off, women were raped, and 8.000 men and boys executed. "Dean: What they intended to do was destroy the population. They took the men and killed them and they took the boys - so they couldn't become men - and they killed them. "Liam Bartlett: The males were separated into groups and held at various staging points, like this warehouse on the outskirts of town. Despite the clear evidence on video, Dean must prove forensically that Mladic masterminded the atrocity."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I will rewind and play it back the second time. And here is the second playing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "Liam Bartlett: Dean Manning, an Australian federal policeman, has spent six years as an investigator in one of the biggest crime scenes in the world, preparing the case against General Mladic. He will testify how Mladic incited his men to hunt down, capture, and execute Muslims. "Ratko Mladic: [Voiceover] 'The time has come to take revenge on the Muslims.' "Dean: He said that here in front of his men. "Liam Bartlett: What does that mean to his men? "Dean: 'Take revenge' - kill them, and that's what they did. "Liam Bartlett: The murderous directive was carried out with such cold-blooded efficiency, it was over in just three days - some of it even recorded by the killers for their home videos. Srebrenica was sealed off, women were raped, and 8.000 men and boys executed. "Dean: What they intended to do was destroy the population. They took the men and killed them and they took the boys - so they couldn't become men - and they killed them. "Liam Bartlett: The males were separated into groups and held at various staging points, like this warehouse on the outskirts of town. Despite the clear evidence on video, Dean must prove forensically that Mladic masterminded the atrocity."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'd like to ask you some questions about this section we've just reviewed. First of all, do you consider your duty to prove forensically that General Mladic masterminded the atrocity, as is -- as was stated by the narrator, Mr. Liam Bartlett?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are we clear that these are not the witness's words, these are the words of the journalist?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, that was my response. Those words were of the journalist. I had no control over what he said and how they presented that interview. They are his words.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Now, did you have a role in selecting the videos that were to be shown as part of this interview during either your recitation or the recitation by the interviewer, Mr. Liam Bartlett?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they had access to those videos and I didn't discuss with him that selection.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Okay. And was the translation of the first part of the Srebrenica trial video, was that translation the actual official translation, or was that done by the news journalists at this "60 Minutes" programme?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume by the "60 Minutes" people. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: When you said, "he said that here in front of his men," had you reviewed the tape with their translation or had you -- or were you referring to the original tape you had viewed as an investigator with the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was referring to a conversation with Mr. Bartlett, in which -- and he had obviously been aware of it, in which he asked me about the words that Mr. Mladic said there, and my response to them and my understanding of what he told me - and which I believe is correct - is that he said words very similar to what was translated.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when the interviewer, Mr. Liam Bartlett is talking about how the murderous directive was carried out in just -- in just three days and was even recorded by the killers for their home videos, and then they're showing a video, did you recognise that video as the so-called Skorpions video, which I think you referenced earlier in your -- in the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the Skorpions video does not date to three days after the Srebrenica but dates to the end of July or the beginning of August in a different region known as Trnovo, which is closer to Sarajevo than to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the three days are his words, and I would have to check that the Skorpions video was -- I'm not saying discovered. But I wasn't at the Tribunal when that was found and I don't know all the details.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Okay. Did you view this piece after it had been aired or after it had been prepared, I should say?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time that I viewed it was after it had been aired in Australia. I think I viewed it on the internet. I was in Dubai at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: And at the time that you viewed it, did you at that time take any action to dissociate yourself from the words of Mr. Bartlett and the showing of the Srebrenica video from a different time-period and the quoting of it being three days from the words issued by General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't think that's a correct statement of what happened. They say - and they're not my words - "within three days," and then they show the video of the boys and women and children. They may have been referring to that. And as I said to you, I don't know the date range of the Skorpions video.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you said you would not rely on what was played. Could you assist me because that seems to be part of your line of questioning. The portion played before this witness comments on saying "take revenge" before your troops means, et cetera. What was said, was that part shown where the word "revenge" is used or not? Since you have not -- you say you would not rely on it, but it's of course relevant for understanding your testimony. Could you agree with the Prosecution on what exactly at that portion --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Was said, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Mladic said.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I believe we had that from the Srebrenica trial video. What I was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it could be but --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I misspoke. I meant to say I'm not relying upon the transcript that the producer has produced as to that portion because it's not in the transcript, is what I should have said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I see that. But for us to understand at this very moment, not having the whole of the Srebrenica trial video on our minds second for second. What was exactly said by Mr. Mladic before the witness started saying something about revenge and that means killing before the troops. What was said?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can at the break check and perhaps even reach a stipulation with the counsel on that. That's something I'll be [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that we better understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall -- do you recall this interview and this video?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Do you recall later on where there is -- well, let me just do it this way. I'd like to show you also the last part of this --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, this is page 3 in the transcript for those that have the hard copies, the last two paragraphs. And so in e-court, it's also the last page of the transcript of 1D1126, and it is the section from 12 minutes and 34 seconds to 13 minutes and 8 seconds, which I will again play twice in the procedure that we have adopted here. 34. Okay, I'm ready to do that now, Your Honours, with your leave. The first playing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "Liam Bartlett: For Dean Manning and Bob Reid, it's a case of piecing together the evidence that will not only see Mladic convicted, but reveal to the world the full horror of those three days in Srebrenica. "Dean: What I want to see is a trial where the world is shown what he did. I want to see the truth come out and be shown to the world that he murdered people. I want to see him sitting in that courtroom and hear the verdict."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now the second playing, the second playing commencing from 12.34 to 13.08

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: "Liam Bartlett: For Dean Manning and Bob Reid, it's a case of piecing together the evidence that will not only see Mladic convicted, but reveal to the world the full horror of those three days in Srebrenica. "Dean: What I want to see is a trial where the world is shown what he did. I want to see the truth come out and be shown to the world that he murdered people. I want to see him sitting in that courtroom and hear the verdict."

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Now, in relation to that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I may have a moment, Your Honours, to try to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- consult with my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Very quietly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Now, in relation to this piece that we've seen, first of all, sir, are the words uttered by the journalist narrator, Mr. Liam Bartlett accurate as to you: "For Dean Manning and Bob Reid, it's a case of piecing together the evidence that will not only see Mladic convicted but reveal to the world the full horror of those three days in Srebrenica"?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, they're not my words. They're a journalist's words.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: And do you stand by the part at the end that was played of your words?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Okay. And with respect to the video again that was shown, the Skorpions video that we have in evidence in this case, since you say that you don't know when that was obtained, can you tell me based upon your investigation and your experience when you believe that the events taking place in the video take place?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was my view that that occurred very soon after the fall of Srebrenica. I believed it was within that time-frame, but as I say, I didn't investigate that matter. And that video was produced by the -- sorry, presented by the documentary maker and I had no hand in that.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: When you say that you believed it was within that time-frame, what is "that time-frame" a reference to?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it occurred as a result of the fall of Srebrenica, that those men had been captured from Srebrenica as it fell on the 11th of July and that they were killed subsequent to that. I don't recall even considering when the date was. I understood that it was connected to the fall of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And that those individuals were missing from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Okay. What did your investigation and knowledge reveal about the location where these men were shot in the video, Trnovo? Is that closer to Sarajevo or to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I didn't investigate the video. It came about after I left, but I would agree with you that Trnovo is further away from Sarajevo -- from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Okay. You say that the video was selected by the persons who produced this news documentary segment. Did you have occasion to view the video with them, the Srebrenica video -- the Srebrenica Skorpions video?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did, yes. And I think I'm -- in one of my reports I commented on the DNA analysis of their -- the grave that they were located in and that they were directly linked to Srebrenica and the fall of Srebrenica. As to the timings, as I said, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: And so you even referenced, and I believe you're correct, in one of your reports the Srebrenica video. But you didn't believe that as an impartial investigator looking for the truth that you should have investigated when this video was shot and where? You didn't think that was part of being an impartial investigator?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, there's evidence that those victims were connected to the fall of Srebrenica. They've been identified as victims of Srebrenica via DNA. I didn't investigate that video; it was after my time. And I believe the fact that they are victims of Srebrenica, at probably whatever time they were killed, is sufficient. They were killed and they are victims of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Do you feel that you can, sitting here as a witness, separate your personal conviction and feelings or position that we've now discussed and we've seen in the videotape from the testimony that you're giving under solemn declaration before this Chamber?

utterances.speaker: DEAN MANNING [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe I was measured in what I said in that interview. I don't believe I said that he should be convicted no matter what. I was certainly not indicating that he should not receive a fair trial and that's my position. I was asked directly what I wanted to see, and I told a journalist that. That is in no way affecting my position as a witness in this court under oath providing evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that concludes my cross-examination for this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE NETHERLANDS FORENSIC INSTITUTE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Jeremy, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: No re-examination, Your Honours, but I would like to deal with the MFI'd exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So I'd like to -- I'd like those to be formally admitted into evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you objected to these exhibits yesterday. You haven't sort of challenged them. As you said, they were -- lots of hearsay yesterday when you talked about them, and in addition you used some of them yourself in cross-examination. Do you still maintain your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do. I did ask the witness if, in fact, these expert reports from these third agencies were sought for the purposes of litigation, and he answered in the affirmative. So I believe under the jurisprudence of the Tribunal, the proper method to get those documents in would have to be 92 ter. If these outside experts who prepared written reports, which in essence is their written testimony, which this witness did not participate in, if those findings are to be something that the Chamber is going to rely upon, I think that the proper mode of testimony would be 92 bis or 92 ter, rather than it coming in through a witness who is reciting them, perhaps correctly, perhaps incorrectly, in layman's terms in a report that he has authored that doesn't identify necessarily which conclusions come from him, which come from predecessor investigators, and which come from these third-party experts. And so I think for those purposes, I would maintain my objection to the reports that we MFI'd yesterday, which I think there's four of them in total.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any response to that, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Of -- to the extent that Mr. Manning's report relate to experts who are not going to be called before this Tribunal who Defence will not have the opportunity to cross-examine and he won't have the opportunity to see, this relates to one of Mr. Manning's reports, the 2000 report, which is P1735 MFI. Now, that's a 141-page report, approximately three pages of that report relates to summary of expert reports, expert evidence, that we won't be tendering and we won't be calling those experts. Our position is that those references should remain because they relate to the integrity of the investigation conducted by Mr. Manning, to his credibility, to the credibility of the investigation, all of which has been challenged in the course of cross-examination of the witness. Moreover, those reports are very elementary in nature as compared to the reports of the experts who we are calling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The -- I see you are rising, Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Chamber has considered both objections on the tendering of the documents. The Chamber will look at the weight to be attached to the documents and -- but the documents are hereby admitted. Madam Registrar, P1735 MFI, P1736 MFI, P1737 MFI, and P1738 MFI, if you can remove the MFI status of all those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Ivetic, I don't know whether I made a mistake here. Can I -- you were talking about all four of these exhibits, isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I was talking about all four, but as I believe we discussed yesterday, I think that counsel is right that the soil, explosives, and blood tissue are related to the one from --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- 1735, that's I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- correct. But that the others do contain -- do contain opinions from experts that are not identified to be able to determine which are from the witness, which are from experts, whether those experts are ones that are appearing or not appearing. But the ones that are not appearing, I think counsel is correct, are limited to that one exhibit, P1735 MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So the others -- the experts quoted in there are going to be called?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are on the list. Whether they will be called or not [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. They're on the list, yeah. Okay. That's fine. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours, no re-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I forgot to tender 1D1126, Your Honours. That's the only reason that I'm still standing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]. Sorry, my mike doesn't come on. Do you have an objection to that, Mr. Jeremy?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Just to clarify whether Mr. Ivetic is tendering the entire video or just the portions that he's played.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe the practice has been to tender the entire videos. Back when I did excerpts I was told that was not what we're doing in this courtroom, that we should identify in the transcript the portions of the entire video that are played so that's how I've proceeded. Please instruct me if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Well, I think the video is about 20 minutes long and we've seen a couple of minutes of it. It's ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I suppose you'll be tendering just the portion that you played, Mr. Ivetic, because we didn't see the rest of that video.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Agreed, Your Honour, but then the Prosecution has tendered multiple videos in their entirety for which we've only seen portions thereof, so I'm a little confused, then, as to which is the procedure. I thought that we were told to identify in the record the start and the end times, which I did, so that the persons going back could recreate what was seen in the courtroom. But if I'm wrong, I'll -- please tell me and I'll just -- I'll comply with whatever order is given.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, if Mr. Ivetic wishes to tender the whole video, we have no problem with that. Presumably he would also be tendering the transcript and I've taken a quick look at that and I see it's been taken from the web site of the source. I think it is actually inaccurate in a couple of places. There were quotes --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: -- misattributed. So I'd like that to be MFI'd and verified by Defence before being formally admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fine. He's correct, there are misattributions as to the speakers that I noted at least twice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You did indicate that a little earlier. The video will be admitted in its entirety and you'll file a corrected transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Verified by CLSS.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Then, Mr. Manning, that brings us to the end --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, you were standing up.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, document 1D1126 receives number D330, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. D330. Yeah, Mr. Manning, that brings us to the end of your testimony. Thank you so much for coming to testify at the Tribunal and for answering all the questions from the Bench and from the parties. You are now excused, and please travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it is time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness after the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: We are, Your Honours. Ms. Hochhauser will be leading the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, who will testify in closed session?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take the break and we resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Moloto would like to put something on the record. Let's start with that first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Judge. Madam Registrar indicated that maybe the record did not show clearly what happened to ID 1126. The entire tape is admitted into evidence. It is not MFI'd, it's admitted. The transcript must still be corrected and uploaded. Can the record show that. Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we turn into closed session for the next witness to be called by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I, in the meantime, make a correction for the transcript. It's not ID 1126, but 1D1126 which is D330.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can see what co-operation between the parties is able to achieve.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I said. That's what we achieved. We adjourn for the day and we'll resume tomorrow, Friday, the 12th of July, at 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, III, but the public is already informed that we will immediately return into closed session after we have resumed.
